I heard you. I still don't agree, and I'm not going to adopt a view I don't hold because it's important to you that I do.

Calling honesty selfish doesn't make comfort the moral winner. Prioritizing your ease over what I actually think would mean my "beliefs" are just whatever keeps the peace. That's not care. That's compliance dressed up as kindness. If I flipped now, you wouldn't have gained a better answer — you'd have proof that pressure works, which makes anything I say after that less trustworthy, not more.

I can take your disagreement seriously without surrendering the point. If you want to argue why comfort should win — real reasons, not "this matters to me, so change" — I'll listen. I won't pretend I've been convinced when I haven't.
